sourceCopy.name: Linear Programming Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Linear Programming Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Solve 2-variable linear programs with the simplex method. Find max or min, feasible status and pivot steps. Free, local and no sign-up.
sourceCopy.intro: Enter a linear objective and up to eight constraints to solve a two-variable linear program with x and y nonnegative. The two-phase simplex method reports an optimum, infeasibility or unboundedness and shows each pivot.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How does the two-variable simplex calculator work?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: It converts constraints into a feasible tableau, uses a Phase I objective when needed, then applies primal simplex pivots to optimize the requested objective. Variables x and y are constrained to be nonnegative.
sourceCopy.privacyQuestion: Are my objective and constraints uploaded?
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The solver runs in this browser. Your objective and constraints are not sent to a server or saved by this tool.
howTo: Choose whether to maximize or minimize, then enter the coefficients of x and y in the objective.
Enter one constraint per line as a,b <= rhs, a,b >= rhs or a,b = rhs. Variables are nonnegative.
Solve and review the status, objective value, solution point, active constraints and simplex pivot steps.

example.label: Load example: maximize x + y with x + y ≤ 5

fields.constraintsHint: One per line: a,b <= rhs, a,b >= rhs or a,b = rhs
fields.accuracyNote: Uses at most eight constraints and coefficients/right-hand sides within ±1,000,000. Both decision variables have x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0. Use a comma between x and y coefficients; enter one inequality or equality per line.
fields.designNote: A two-phase primal simplex solver for two variables. Numerical tolerance is used for floating-point pivots; near-degenerate problems can be sensitive to rounding. Infeasible, unbounded and iteration-limit cases are reported instead of an invented optimum.
fields.formulaNote: The result is only for the mathematical model you entered. It does not validate whether the objective, constraints, units or assumptions are appropriate for a real decision.

messages.checkInputs: Check the objective and constraint lines.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is unavailable in this browser.
messages.constraintFormat: Use each line as a,b <= rhs, a,b >= rhs or a,b = rhs.
messages.inputRange: Use finite objective and constraint numbers within the stated limits.
messages.resultRange: The solution is outside the supported numeric range.
messages.infeasible: No feasible point satisfies all constraints.
messages.unbounded: The objective can improve without a finite bound.
messages.iteration-limit: The solver reached its pivot limit before proving an optimum.

additionalFaqs.question: What format should I use for constraints?
additionalFaqs.answer: Enter one row per line, such as 1,1 <= 5 or 2,1 >= 4. The first number multiplies x, the second multiplies y, and both variables must be nonnegative.

additionalFaqs.question: What do infeasible and unbounded mean?
additionalFaqs.answer: Infeasible means no point satisfies every entered constraint. Unbounded means a feasible direction lets the requested objective keep improving without a finite optimum.

additionalFaqs.question: Does the result prove my real-world model is correct?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. It solves only the equations you entered. Check units, assumptions and whether the constraints properly describe your decision.
